verbalization: Lucensimycin D is shown to interact with the Prostaglandin D2 receptor, which is a target of two distinct compounds: (1S,18R,20S,21S,22S)-6,7,8,11,12,13,21,22-octahydroxy-3,16-dioxo-2,17,19-trioxatetracyclo[16.3.1.0^{4,9}.0^{10,15}]docosa-4(9),5,7,10,12,14-hexaen-20-yl 3,4,5-trihydroxybenzoate and 9-Hydroxy-12-oxo-10-octadecenoic acid. Both of these compounds are implicated in the targeting of Multidrug resistance-associated protein 7, suggesting a potential mechanism by which Lucensimycin D may exert its effects. The shared targeting of the Prostaglandin D2 receptor by these compounds implies a possible common pathway or a shared biological function. The evidence suggests that Lucensimycin D may act through a mechanism involving the Prostaglandin D2 receptor, which is involved in the regulation of multidrug resistance. The integration of these findings supports the hypothesis that Lucensimycin D may modulate the expression or activity of Multidrug resistance-associated protein 7, potentially through the Prostaglandin D2 receptor. The mechanism is supported by the direct interaction of Lucensimycin D with the receptor and the subsequent targeting of the protein by other compounds, indicating a possible role in the modulation of multidrug resistance.
